excerpt: Naise AI is a Singapore-built marketing agent that runs social media, influencer and PR work from one brief. Pricing from $59.90/month, alternatives and launch-day questions.
content:
Naise AI (pronounced "nice") is a marketing tool that tries to do the work as well as suggest it. It has three agents: a social media agent that finds trending topics, drafts posts and images and schedules them on a content calendar; an influencer agent for finding creators, checking for fake followers and tracking campaign deliverables; and a PR agent that builds media lists and monitors news about your brand. It keeps a memory of your brand guidelines and tone so that you do not have to explain them in every prompt.

Two free tools sit at the front: a social audit that grades an Instagram profile on its last 30 posts, and a brand audit that crawls a website for brand, SEO and AI-search gaps. Nothing is published until you approve it, co-founder Roy Kek said on Product Hunt, and agencies can run several brands as separate workspaces in one account. The company says it is headquartered in Singapore.

Naise AI launched on Product Hunt on 23 September 2026 and finished #2 for the day, with 366 upvotes and 84 comments (as of 14 October 2026).

We have not tested Naise AI ourselves. This page brings together its official site, pricing, About and contact pages and its Product Hunt page, and says where each fact comes from.

use_cases: Auditing an Instagram profile or a brand's website before planning content
Building a month's content calendar, captions and images from one brief
Finding influencers and tracking what they deliver
Building a media list and monitoring news coverage of your brand
Running several client brands from one agency account

paragraphs: Co-founder Roy Kek pitched Naise AI at people who know their business but not what their social media should say: which content pillars, which topics, and how to turn attention into customers.

He described a loop: learn the brand, research competitors, trends and news, work out which hooks and formats perform, create scripts, captions and images, then schedule and learn from results. He said it connects directly to social accounts and uses models focused on marketing data.
launch_story.attribution: Roy Kek, co-founder, on Product Hunt

fit: are a founder or small team without a marketing hire
run an agency with several client brands and want them in separate workspaces
want social, influencer and PR work in one tool instead of several
not_fit: need audience-overlap analysis for influencers: Roy Kek said on Product Hunt it is not available yet
want approvals in Slack or Teams: approval currently happens in the Naise dashboard, with chat integration on the roadmap
do not want to add a card for a trial: the free trial needs one and billing starts automatically

pricing.intro: Every plan includes all the agents; plans differ by campaigns per month and AI usage. Prices are Naise AI's, in US dollars.

plans.name: Entry
plans.detail: 2 campaigns a month, standard AI usage, unlimited creator reach and outreach

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.detail: Higher volumes, more markets or custom terms

notes: Every plan starts with a 3-day free trial. You add a card to begin, and billing starts automatically unless you cancel before it ends.
The social audit and brand audit can be run free after signing up with a verified email.

pros: All agents are included in every plan
Keeps a persistent memory of your brand voice
Nothing is published without your approval, according to the co-founder
Multiple brands per account for agencies
cons: Trial needs a card and converts automatically
Approvals only inside the dashboard for now

liked: Usefulness for people creating content for several brands
asked: Whether there is an approval step before posting (yes, in the dashboard)
Whether agencies can manage several brands in one account (yes, as workspaces)
Whether it detects fake followers (in the pipeline, said the co-founder; the site now lists a fake follower checker)
How it works for small niches such as immigration (you can add specific competitors to benchmark against)

quotes.text: I create content for a few brands, Naise could come in handy.
quotes.author: Raghav Mehra

alternatives.intro: These are products Product Hunt lists as Naise AI alternatives. Review scores are Product Hunt users' own.

items.name: Publer
items.what: Create, schedule and analyse social posts on one platform
items.difference: A scheduling tool you drive yourself; Naise adds research, influencer and PR agents.

items.name: STORI
items.what: AI that builds your inbound channels
items.difference: Focused on inbound content; Naise also covers influencer outreach and PR.

items.name: Blaze
items.difference: A similar all-in-one AI marketing pitch; compare channels covered and approval controls.

alternatives.more: Product Hunt also lists Narrato and Highperformr.ai as alternatives.

x.none: We found no posts about Naise AI on X to link yet.

faq.a: An AI marketing tool with social media, influencer and PR agents that research, draft, schedule and report from one brief, while remembering your brand voice. It is built in Singapore.

faq.q: How much does Naise AI cost?
faq.a: Entry is $59.90 a month ($45.90 billed annually), Middle $119 ($89.90 annually) and Advanced $199 ($149.90 annually). Every plan has a 3-day free trial that needs a card.

faq.q: Does Naise AI post without my approval?
faq.a: No. Co-founder Roy Kek said on Product Hunt that nothing is published until you or your team approve it in the dashboard.

faq.q: Can an agency manage several brands?
faq.a: Yes. Each brand gets its own workspace within one account, according to the co-founder.

faq.q: Does Naise AI work for niche industries?
faq.a: The co-founder said you can add specific competitors or adjacent accounts to benchmark against when there is little general content in your niche.

faq.q: What are the alternatives to Naise AI?
faq.a: Product Hunt lists STORI, Blaze, Publer, Narrato and Highperformr.ai.
